**Status:** The repo is archived and no longer maintained. The page says it "was archived by the owner on Apr 3, 2026. It is now read-only."

**Built-in Studio MCP server:** The README says the team has "shifted ongoing engineering investment to the built-in MCP Server included with Roblox Studio," which it recommends for connecting external AI tools. This server remains available for reference and existing workflows.

**Tools exposed:**
- run_code
- insert_model
- get_console_output
- start_stop_play
- run_script_in_play_mode
- get_studio_mode

**Install on Windows:**
1. Download `rbx-studio-mcp.exe` from the latest release.
2. Run it. The page's quick setup then says to restart your AI client and Roblox Studio.
3. For manual setup, add an MCP config entry whose command points to the downloaded `.exe` with the argument `--stdio`.

**Claude Desktop:** Open Settings > Developer > Edit Config to find `claude_desktop_config.json`, then add the config entry above. The page says the installer sets up Claude Desktop and Cursor automatically if they're found.

**Claude Code:** Run:
`claude mcp add --transport stdio Roblox_Studio -- '<path-to-rbx-studio-mcp>' --stdio`
The page gives a macOS example path (`/Applications/RobloxStudioMCP.app/Contents/MacOS/rbx-studio-mcp`) but no Windows path for this command.

**Latest release date:** Not stated. The page's Releases section is empty in the captured content, so I can't tell from it.

**Current version:** v2.7.0-next.6, described as 43 tools, an inspector edition, and a monorepo architecture.

**Tools:** The page doesn't list the 43 full-edition tools. It lists 31 read-only inspector tools, grouped loosely here:
- **Files and scripts:** `get_file_tree`, `search_files`, `get_script_source`, `grep_scripts`, `get_project_structure`
- **Instances and properties:** `get_place_info`, `get_services`, `search_objects`, `get_instance_properties`, `get_instance_children`, `search_by_property`, `get_class_info`, `mass_get_property`, `get_attributes`, `get_tags`, `get_tagged`, `get_selection`, `get_connected_instances`, `get_descendants`, `compare_instances`
- **Output and playtest:** `get_playtest_output`, `get_output_log`
- **Build and library:** `export_build`, `list_library`, `search_materials`, `get_build`
- **Assets:** `search_assets`, `get_asset_details`, `get_asset_thumbnail`, `preview_asset`
- **Screenshots:** `capture_screenshot`

**Your specific categories:**
- **Execute Luau:** Not mentioned.
- **Insert assets:** Not mentioned. The inspector edition only searches and previews assets.
- **Build/mass create:** Not mentioned as a tool. The page gives "Create 50 test NPCs in a grid" as an example request only.
- **Animation:** Not mentioned.
- **Camera:** Not mentioned.
- **Screenshots:** `capture_screenshot` is in the inspector list.

**Claude Code install (full edition):**
```
claude mcp add robloxstudio -- npx -y robloxstudio-mcp@latest
```
For the inspector edition: `claude mcp add robloxstudio-inspector -- npx -y robloxstudio-mcp-inspector@latest`

Also install the Studio plugin and enable "Allow HTTP Requests" in Experience Settings > Security.

**Windows notes:** If you have issues, run the server through `cmd`. In an MCP client config, set `"command": "cmd"` with args `["/c", "npx", "-y", "robloxstudio-mcp@latest"]`.

**Latest release date:** Not stated on the page.

**License:** MIT.

**Important:** The repository was archived by its owner on June 6, 2026, and is now read-only. The owner recommends the actively maintained fork at github.com/Chrrxs/robloxstudio-mcp.

- **Roblox Video Stars:** Roblox runs a creator program that gives participants benefits and tools to engage fans and monetize on Roblox. It requires transparency about the relationship with Roblox, and it notes that third-party platform rules and local laws may add requirements. (help.roblox.com/hc/articles/360026092011)
- **Roblox's own uploads:** Creator Hub lets developers upload gameplay videos directly for their game pages, replacing YouTube embeds. The announcement says uploads should show authentic, current gameplay. (devforum.roblox.com, thread on removing YouTube videos from game detail pages, dated for September 30, 2026)
- **YouTube's side:** YouTube's monetization rules require original content, and gaming videos that mostly show extended gameplay can run into limits. Gaming creators also have to follow the policies of each game publisher. (support.google.com/youtube/answer/2490020; vidiq.com)
- **Other publisher policies:** One result describes a different game company's policy allowing monetized YouTube gameplay videos as long as they follow its guidelines. This is not a Roblox policy, so don't treat it as one. (rokaplay.helpscoutdocs.com)
- **Roblox ad-rewards:** A third-party blog quotes Roblox as requiring that these videos show "real in-game gameplay without misleading edits." It's unverified and doesn't cover monetized YouTube uploads. (lastlevel.pages.dev)

To confirm the actual rule, check Roblox's Terms of Use and Community Standards directly, and the Creator Hub or Video Stars pages for current guidance.

YouTube's July 15, 2025 change renamed its "repetitious content" policy to "inauthentic content," and it does not ban AI voices or TTS outright. The risk is in how the narration is used. These findings come from third-party blogs and guides, not YouTube's own Help Center, which didn't appear in the results.

- **The rename:** YouTube renamed its former "repetitious content" policy to "inauthentic content" on July 15, 2025.
- **TTS is not banned:** One source says the update does not ban AI voiceovers or text-to-speech (TTS). Another notes that YouTube does not prohibit synthetic narration or text-to-speech simply because the voice was created with AI.
- **What gets flagged:** YouTube's examples include text-to-speech voiceovers reading non-original text and slideshows with minimal or no original commentary. A guide adds that the key question is original work versus automated, interchangeable content.
- **Practical guidance:** One source advises creators to avoid using existing clips or text-to-speech narrations (especially if those are AI-generated) when making tutorials and vlogs, and to incorporate value through commentary and editing.

Caveat: the sources conflict on tone. Some describe the change as a clarification of existing rules, which one says have made mass-produced and inauthentic content ineligible for monetization for years. Others describe it as a crackdown. Several results are dated 2026, so they may reflect later guidance. Confirm the current wording against YouTube's official channel monetization policy page before relying on this.

**Current version:** The page doesn't give this release's version. It says the project is "Based on boshyxd/robloxstudio-mcp v2.7.0," which is the upstream base. Check the Releases section or the npm package for the current version.

**Last update:** Not shown. The repo has 190 commits, but the page has no date.

**Number of tools:** Not stated. The page links to a "complete tool list" in `packages/core/src/tools/definitions.ts`.

**Tool categories listed on the page:**
- **Debug a running game:** `eval_server_runtime`, `eval_client_runtime`, `breakpoints`, `get_runtime_logs`
- **Automate playtests:** `solo_playtest`, `multiplayer_playtest`, `manage_instance`
- **Find performance problems:** `capture_script_profiler`, `capture_micro_profiler`, `get_memory_breakdown`, `get_scene_analysis`
- **Work in edit mode:** `execute_luau`, `set_properties`, `find_and_replace_in_scripts`, `selection`, `capture_screenshot`, plus mouse and keyboard input
- **Inspect Creator Store assets:** `search_assets`, `get_asset_details`, `preview_asset`, `insert_asset`
- **Manage monetization:** `manage_monetization`
- **Manage experience settings:** `manage_experience`
- **Look up Roblox APIs:** `get_roblox_docs`, `get_roblox_skills`

Your requested categories are only partly covered. Execute Luau, insert assets, playtest, and screenshot appear above. The page doesn't list dedicated tools for creating objects, animation, or camera. `selection` can frame a part or model before a screenshot, and `execute_luau` handles project-specific edits, but neither is a named camera or object-creation tool.

**Install command for Claude Code:**
```
claude mcp add robloxstudio -- npx -y @chrrxs/robloxstudio-mcp@latest --auto-install-plugin
```
The read-only Inspector edition uses `robloxstudio-inspector` and `@chrrxs/robloxstudio-mcp-inspector@latest`. Install only one variant at a time.

**Windows notes:** The page has no Windows-specific section. The general setup applies: "Fully close and reopen Studio after installation or updates." The plugin shows **Connected** when it is ready. You can set `MCP_PLUGINS_DIR` to use a custom plugins folder. The Wine section covers native Linux, not Windows.

# Roblox Studio MCP Server

## Enable the server
1. Open **Assistant**.
2. Click **…** → **Manage MCP Servers**.
3. Turn on **Enable Studio as MCP server**.

A green indicator shows how many clients are connected.

## Supported clients
- **Quick connect:** Antigravity, Codex CLI, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Visual Studio Code
- **Other clients:** Any client that supports `stdio` transport, using a JSON config or CLI command.

## Connecting Claude Code and Claude Desktop
The source doesn't give client-specific commands or config file paths for these two. Options:
- **Quick connect:** In **Assistant Settings** → **MCP Servers**, expand **Quick connect** and turn on your client. If it doesn't appear, install it and restart Roblox Studio.
- **JSON configuration:** Add the following to your client's MCP config. If you already have other servers, add only the `Roblox_Studio` entry to your existing `mcpServers` dictionary, separated by a comma.

  Windows:
  ```json
  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "Roblox_Studio": {
        "command": "cmd.exe",
        "args": ["/c", "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Roblox\\mcp.bat"]
      }
    }
  }
  ```

  macOS:
  ```json
  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "Roblox_Studio": {
        "command": "/Applications/RobloxStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/StudioMCP"
      }
    }
  }
  ```

- **CLI command** (if your client requires one):

  Windows: `cmd.exe /c %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\mcp.bat`

  macOS: `/Applications/RobloxStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/StudioMCP`

After configuring, restart the client.

## Tools

**Scripts**
- `script_read`: Reads a script by dot-notation path, entire or by line range.
- `multi_edit`: Applies multiple edits in one operation; creates the script if the path doesn't exist. Requires `datamodel_type`.
- `script_search`: Fuzzy-searches scripts by name, up to 10 results.
- `script_grep`: Searches all scripts for a string pattern, up to 50 matches.

**Asset and content generation**
- `generate_animation`: Creates an R15 animation from a text prompt, or converts an R6 animation to R15 by asset ID. Duration up to 10 seconds.
- `generate_mesh`: Generates a textured 3D mesh from a text prompt.
- `generate_material`: Generates a custom material variant.
- `generate_procedural_model`: Builds a ProceduralModel from primitive parts, with optional reference images and custom part schemas.
- `wait_job_finished`: Waits for a procedural model job and returns its final status.
- `search_asset`: Searches the Creator Store and Creator Inventory, with filters for type, price, tags, and scope.
- `insert_asset`: Inserts an asset by numeric asset ID.
- `upload_image`: Uploads images from HTTP URLs and returns a path-to-asset-ID map.
- `store_image`: Loads a local image file and returns a URI for other tools.

**Data model exploration**
- `subagent`: Launches an `explore` or `playtest` subagent for multi-step tasks.
- `search_game_tree`: Explores the instance hierarchy as a flat JSON array, with filters and depth limits.
- `inspect_instance`: Returns an instance's properties, attributes, and a summary of its children and descendants.

**Luau execution**
- `execute_luau`: Runs Luau in Edit, Client, or Server datamodel and returns the result or error.

**Playtesting**
- `get_studio_state`: Returns play state and available datamodel types.
- `start_stop_play`: Starts or stops playtesting.
- `get_console_output`: Retrieves the Studio output log.
- `screen_capture`: Captures the viewport, with optional camera position and look-at target.

**Player input simulation**
- `character_navigation`: Moves the player character to a position or instance, with a speed multiplier.
- `user_keyboard_input`: Sends ordered key down/up/press, text input, or wait actions.
- `user_mouse_input`: Sends ordered move, click, button down/up, scroll, or wait actions.

**Documentation and skills**
- `http_get`: Fetches allowed Roblox documentation pages, with keyword search.
- `skill`: Retrieves reference material for skills such as debugging and device simulation.

**Place management**
- `save_place`: Saves the open place, like **File** → **Save**, without opening dialogs.

**Session management**
- `list_roblox_studios`: Lists connected Studio instances with name, instance ID, and place ID.

**Feedback**
- `submit_feedback`: Sends feedback to Roblox about failed tools, missing capabilities, or excessive workflow steps.

Every tool call requires a `studio_id` to target a specific instance. Use `list_roblox_studios` to find it.

## Limitations
- Requires the latest version of Roblox Studio and an installed MCP client.
- Communication uses `stdio` transport, with the server running as a local process.
- Calling Open Cloud APIs without an API key requires a separate guide.
- Playtest teleport testing has limitations. See the linked teleport documentation.
- Tool-specific limits are listed above, such as result caps and the 10-second animation duration.

## Security warning
MCP clients can read and modify content in your open Roblox places. Only connect clients you trust.

## Troubleshooting
- Restart both Roblox Studio and the MCP client.
- Confirm the command or binary path exists.
- Check the JSON syntax, including commas and brackets.

- **Quick connect:** In **Assistant Settings** → **MCP Servers**, expand **Quick connect** and turn on your client. If it doesn't appear, install it and restart Roblox Studio.
- **JSON configuration:** Add the following to your client's MCP config. If you already have other servers, add only the `Roblox_Studio` entry to your existing `mcpServers` dictionary, separated by a comma.

  Windows:
  ```json
  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "Roblox_Studio": {
        "command": "cmd.exe",
        "args": ["/c", "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Roblox\\mcp.bat"]
      }
    }
  }
  ```

  macOS:
  ```json
  {
    "mcpServers": {
      "Roblox_Studio": {
        "command": "/Applications/RobloxStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/StudioMCP"
      }
    }
  }
  ```

- **CLI command** (if your client requires one):

  Windows: `cmd.exe /c %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\mcp.bat`

  macOS: `/Applications/RobloxStudio.app/Contents/MacOS/StudioMCP`

After configuring, restart the client.

## Tools

**Scripts**
- `script_read`: Reads a script by dot-notation path, entire or by line range.
- `multi_edit`: Applies multiple edits in one operation; creates the script if the path doesn't exist. Requires `datamodel_type`.
- `script_search`: Fuzzy-searches scripts by name, up to 10 results.
- `script_grep`: Searches all scripts for a string pattern, up to 50 matches.

**Asset and content generation**
- `generate_animation`: Creates an R15 animation from a text prompt, or converts an R6 animation to R15 by asset ID. Duration up to 10 seconds.
- `generate_mesh`: Generates a textured 3D mesh from a text prompt.
- `generate_material`: Generates a custom material variant.
- `generate_procedural_model`: Builds a ProceduralModel from primitive parts, with optional reference images and custom part schemas.
- `wait_job_finished`: Waits for a procedural model job and returns its final status.
- `search_asset`: Searches the Creator Store and Creator Inventory, with filters for type, price, tags, and scope.
- `insert_asset`: Inserts an asset by numeric asset ID.
- `upload_image`: Uploads images from HTTP URLs and returns a path-to-asset-ID map.
- `store_image`: Loads a local image file and returns a URI for other tools.

**Data model exploration**
- `subagent`: Launches an `explore` or `playtest` subagent for multi-step tasks.
- `search_game_tree`: Explores the instance hierarchy as a flat JSON array, with filters and depth limits.
- `inspect_instance`: Returns an instance's properties, attributes, and a summary of its children and descendants.

**Luau execution**
- `execute_luau`: Runs Luau in Edit, Client, or Server datamodel and returns the result or error.

**Playtesting**
- `get_studio_state`: Returns play state and available datamodel types.
- `start_stop_play`: Starts or stops playtesting.
- `get_console_output`: Retrieves the Studio output log.
- `screen_capture`: Captures the viewport, with optional camera position and look-at target.

**Player input simulation**
- `character_navigation`: Moves the player character to a position or instance, with a speed multiplier.
- `user_keyboard_input`: Sends ordered key down/up/press, text input, or wait actions.
- `user_mouse_input`: Sends ordered move, click, button down/up, scroll, or wait actions.

**Documentation and skills**
- `http_get`: Fetches allowed Roblox documentation pages, with keyword search.
- `skill`: Retrieves reference material for skills such as debugging and device simulation.

**Place management**
- `save_place`: Saves the open place, like **File** → **Save**, without opening dialogs.

**Session management**
- `list_roblox_studios`: Lists connected Studio instances with name, instance ID, and place ID.

**Feedback**
- `submit_feedback`: Sends feedback to Roblox about failed tools, missing capabilities, or excessive workflow steps.

Every tool call requires a `studio_id` to target a specific instance. Use `list_roblox_studios` to find it.

## Limitations
- Requires the latest version of Roblox Studio and an installed MCP client.
- Communication uses `stdio` transport, with the server running as a local process.
- Calling Open Cloud APIs without an API key requires a separate guide.
- Playtest teleport testing has limitations. See the linked teleport documentation.
- Tool-specific limits are listed above, such as result caps and the 10-second animation duration.

## Security warning
MCP clients can read and modify content in your open Roblox places. Only connect clients you trust.

## Troubleshooting
- Restart both Roblox Studio and the MCP client.
- Confirm the command or binary path exists.
- Check the JSON syntax, including commas and brackets.

The search turned up no DevForum or Reddit threads. The results are mostly setup guides, vendor pages, and a few first-person accounts, so treat the experience reports as anecdotal.

**Setup:** Roblox now has an MCP server built into Studio. Roblox shipped an open-source Studio MCP server (May 2025), added playtest tools (February 2026), and in March 2026 built the MCP server into Studio itself. To connect, you enable it under Assistant's MCP settings, and Claude Code and Claude Desktop are both listed as quick-connect clients. Community MCP servers also exist, such as robloxstudio-mcp, which offers 54 tools that give Claude direct access to a running Roblox Studio instance.

**Experience reports:**
- A Medium author built a game with every line of Lua code, every object creation, every property change done through Claude Code connected to Roblox Studio via MCP. Their biggest complaint was that they spent more time debugging visual issues than writing the game logic, since Claude can't see the scene. Their advice was to write a thorough game design document first.
- A Japanese note.com tutorial reported that Claude Desktop used the Roblox Studio MCP tools (using 3 to 5 tools), created two scripts on its own, and even automatically executed a playtest. That was for a simple coin-collection game.

**Limitations:**
- Visual feedback is the main gap, as the Medium account describes.
- A guide notes that the agent can insert Creator Store models, but it can't tell which assets make your game look like your game.
- Its verdict was that a small game, yes. A good game still takes your judgement.
- claude.ai in a browser can help you plan and write Luau but can't connect to Studio.

Overall, the sources support simple-to-medium games built through MCP, with significant human work needed for visuals and polish. Most of this evidence is from 2026 blog posts and guides, not independent reviews.

content.content:
**Free License:** Individuals and companies of up to 3 people qualify. The page describes it as "individuals and companies of up to 3 people," with all features and unlimited commercial use, subject to the Terms. The License FAQ covers eligibility in more detail.

**Company License:** Required if you don't qualify for the Free License. You can choose one or both options:

- **Remotion for Automators:** $0.01 per render, billed in blocks of 1,000 renders ($10), with a $100 monthly minimum. Intended for batch rendering and automated video products.
- **Remotion for Creators:** $25 per month per seat, for low-volume manual video creation and local motion design work.

Developers working on automation projects don't need a Creators seat.

The thread doesn't cover recording, rendering, or editing software. Its suggestions fall into these areas:

**Animators**
- **Moon Animator** (a Roblox Studio plugin): one commenter recommended it and suggested watching its updated tutorial. It is now paid.
- **Blender**: suggested as an option for creating animations outside Studio.
- **Default Animator**: the original poster says it works well. They wrote that "moon animator is hella overrated" and that they "used the default animator just fine."
- **Free animator plugins**: a commenter suggested searching the Creator Marketplace for free options.

**Camera and cutscenes**
- Scripting the cameras yourself, with precise timing, is the method the original poster used.
- Cutscene scripting or cutscene plugins were also suggested.

**Effects**
- Welding parts and adding effects such as particles, sparkles, and "boom" explosions.

**Learning resources**
- YouTube tutorials on the topic, learned gradually.

Based on the tutorial, the process works like this:

1. **Set up the rig:** Place any rig in the workspace.
2. **Get the face IDs:** Find the face images in the Toolbox, right-click the one you want, and copy its ID. Keep your normal face ID handy.
3. **Create the animation:** Open Moon Animator from the plugin menu and create a new animation. Name it, add your rig, and enable "Include Marker Track."
4. **Animate the body:** Add any movement you want, such as head shakes.
5. **Add the marker track:** Open the Markers panel, add the track, and open the marker editor (the backtick key or the track's edit option).
6. **Script the face changes:** The tutorial doesn't keyframe the Texture property directly. Instead, it uses a script placed where the "Code Begin" note is. The script sets the head's face decal Texture to your normal face ID first, then to each alternate face ID, with `wait()` calls between changes.
7. **Customize the script:** Replace the NPC name and face texture name placeholders with your rig's names. Put each face ID in its own line, add more lines for more changes, and adjust the wait times to fit your timing.

content.text:
# Informe: producción de shorts animados de Roblox tipo R6Rants con Claude

**Aviso previo:** desde esta máquina la red (Fortinet) bloquea `create.roblox.com` y `en.help.roblox.com` ("Web Page Blocked", categoría bloqueada). `devforum.roblox.com` sí cargó. Leí la documentación oficial por su espejo en GitHub. Es probable que Roblox Studio tampoco funcione en esta red, así que pruébalo antes de planear.

## 1. Cómo se hacen estos videos

- **No pude verificar el flujo exacto de R6Rants.** No encontré ningún tutorial ni declaración del canal. Los resultados sobre "Roblox rants" describen otro formato (gameplay grabado con voz IA y subtítulos), no animación. https://clippie.ai/blog/how-to-make-roblox-rant-videos-2026
- **Moon Animator 2:** es el plugin estándar de la comunidad para animación cinemática (personajes, cámara, luces y propiedades). Es de pago; la cifra más repetida es 29.99 USD de pago único, pero viene de fuentes secundarias y no pude abrir la ficha oficial. https://thetoolstrunk.com/how-much-is-moon-animator/ y https://www.roblox.com/communities/5677095/Moon-Animator
- **Animation Editor integrado:** es gratis y varios creadores dicen que alcanza. En el DevForum recomiendan el editor por defecto con cámaras programadas por script, plugins de cutscene, o Blender. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-to-make-roblox-animations-for-trailersyoutube/2572053
- **Grabación:** el método documentado es ocultar la interfaz con Ctrl+H, pantalla completa con F11, grabar con cualquier grabador y recortar. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-to-record-trailers-with-moon-animation-suite/1923201
  - El grabador interno baja la resolución y graba en WMV, por eso se recomienda OBS (gratis). https://devforum.roblox.com/t/the-recording-tools-need-to-be-upgraded-urgently/2823204
  - Sube la calidad de render de Studio para evitar bordes borrosos. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/transparency-issue-moon-animator/838131
  - No encontré un flujo documentado de render cuadro a cuadro ni un visor 9:16 nativo en Studio. Lo habitual es grabar en horizontal y recortar a vertical.
- **Caras en R6:** la cara es un Decal en la cabeza y la expresión se cambia cambiando su `Texture`. Las caras propias se suben como decals. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-to-import-high-quality-character-faces-on-roblox-characters-works-with-r15-and-r6/622433
  - En Moon Animator se hace con un script en la pista de marcadores que cambia el ID de textura. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-to-changeanimate-faces-in-moon-animation-suite/589563
  - Existe un pack de caras 2D con rig para Blender (AltiWyre). https://devforum.roblox.com/t/2d-face-rig-exporter-for-altiwyres-face-pack-blender-40-to-roblox/4818532
- **Avatares y ropa:** el Rig Builder integrado inserta rigs R6 y también tu propio avatar con accesorios. https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/rig-builder
  - Hay plugins "Load Character" que cargan cualquier avatar por nombre de usuario. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/load-character-plugin/1848301
- **Blender:** hay rigs R6 IK/FK con plugin de sincronización hacia Studio. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/r6-ik-fk-blender-rig-v222/3586405
  - No verifiqué el flujo de render final en Blender (Eevee o Cycles). Para tu estilo de tomas simples no lo veo necesario.

## 2. Claude y Roblox Studio (estado a noviembre de 2026)

- **El servidor MCP ya viene integrado en Studio.** El repo `Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server` fue archivado el 3 de abril de 2026 y su README remite al integrado. https://github.com/Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server
- **Activación:** Assistant, menú "…", Manage MCP Servers, activar "Enable Studio as MCP server". En "Quick connect" aparecen Claude Code y Claude Desktop. https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/mcp (espejo: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/studio/mcp.md)
- **Configuración manual en Windows** (JSON del cliente MCP, según la doc oficial):

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "Roblox_Studio": { "command": "cmd.exe", "args": ["/c", "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Roblox\\mcp.bat"] } } }
```

- **Para Claude Code** el equivalente sería `claude mcp add --transport stdio Roblox_Studio -- cmd.exe /c %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\mcp.bat`. Esta línea la deduje de la doc; no la probé.
- **Herramientas útiles para tu caso** (misma doc):
  - `execute_luau`: corre Luau en Edit, Client o Server.
  - `search_asset` e `insert_asset`: buscan e insertan del Creator Store.
  - `generate_procedural_model`, `generate_mesh`, `generate_material`: generan props y materiales.
  - `upload_image` y `store_image`: sirven para subir las caras 2D.
  - `screen_capture`: captura el visor con posición de cámara y punto de mira, así Claude puede revisar el encuadre.
  - `start_stop_play`, `get_console_output`, `save_place`, `multi_edit` y simulación de teclado y mouse.
- **Límite clave:** `generate_animation` solo crea animaciones R15 de hasta 10 segundos (o convierte R6 a R15). No hay herramienta nativa de animación R6 ni de grabación de video.
- **Lo que sí puede hacer Claude** (inferencia mía sobre `execute_luau`, sin ejemplo público que lo confirme):
  - Construir sets con Parts, clima con ParticleEmitter e iluminación.
  - Colocar rigs R6.
  - Escribir un script "director" por toma: cámara scriptable, movimiento con tweens de Motor6D o CFrame, cambio de `Texture` de la cara.
  - Tú reproduces y grabas con OBS.
- **Servidores comunitarios:**
  - `boshyxd/robloxstudio-mcp` fue archivado el 6 de junio de 2026 y remite al fork activo. https://github.com/boshyxd/robloxstudio-mcp
  - El fork `Chrrxs/robloxstudio-mcp` trae `execute_luau`, `insert_asset`, `capture_screenshot` y playtests. Se instala con `claude mcp add robloxstudio -- npx -y @chrrxs/robloxstudio-mcp@latest --auto-install-plugin`. https://github.com/Chrrxs/robloxstudio-mcp
  - También existe un "Animation MCP" comunitario, orientado a animaciones de combate, que no evalué. https://lobehub.com/mcp/thatguythd-animation-mcp
- **Rojo:** no lo verifiqué en esta sesión. Para escenas no es necesario, porque el MCP edita scripts directamente.
- **Ejemplos reales:** solo encontré juegos, no animaciones ni cutscenes.
  - Un autor construyó un juego completo con Claude Code por MCP y dice que gastó más tiempo depurando lo visual que la lógica. https://medium.com/@andy.a.g/i-built-a-roblox-game-using-only-ai-agents-heres-what-happened-ed57b553facc
  - Otras guías: https://luismori.dev/article/roblox-game-development-with-mcp/ y https://forgeblox.app/guides/use-claude-with-roblox-studio

## 3. Voz

- **ElevenLabs** (página oficial): https://elevenlabs.io/pricing

| Plan | Precio al mes | Créditos | Licencia comercial |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 0 USD | 10k (unos 10 min) | No figura |
| Starter | 6 USD (1 USD el primer mes) | 30k (unos 30 min) | Sí |
| Creator | 22 USD (11 USD el primer mes) | 121k (unos 121 min) | Sí |
| Pro | 99 USD | 600k | Sí |

- Con videos de unos 100 segundos, Starter alcanza para unos 15 videos al mes sin contar repeticiones.
- **Voces del género:** no pude verificar cuál usa R6Rants. "Adam" es la voz que ElevenLabs promociona como típica de narración en redes. https://elevenlabs.io/voice-library/adam
- **Alternativas:** grabar tu propia voz (gratis y lo más seguro para monetizar). Kokoro y edge-tts existen como opciones gratuitas, pero no verifiqué sus licencias.
- **Postura de YouTube:** la política oficial no menciona TTS ni voces sintéticas. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1311392
  - Lo que sí veta: "contenido generado con IA con plantillas genéricas que da impresión de producción en masa", historias de plantilla y lecturas de material que no creaste.
  - Lo que permite: usar herramientas creativas para entregar una narrativa única.
  - Desde el 15 de julio de 2025 la política se llama "contenido inauténtico" y no prohíbe las voces IA en sí (fuente secundaria). https://typecast.ai/learn/youtube-ai-monetization-july-15-ypp-update/
  - Riesgo real: guiones genéricos repetidos, no la voz.

## 4. Subtítulos y edición

- **CapCut:** los subtítulos automáticos ya no son ilimitados en el plan gratis y las fuentes se contradicen.
  - Varias hablan de un tope de unos 10 minutos por video; Descript dice que se quitaron del plan gratis en 2025. https://descript.com/blog/article/capcut-captions-arent-free-anymore-heres-a-better-option
  - Precios reportados: Standard 9.99 USD al mes y Pro 19.99 USD al mes, aunque otra fuente dice 7.99. Varían por país y no los verifiqué en la página oficial. https://eesel.ai/blog/capcut-pricing
- **DaVinci Resolve:** la versión gratuita existe; no verifiqué precios ni su función de subtítulos en esta sesión.
- **Opción programática** (la que mejor encaja con Claude Code):
  - WhisperX da marcas de tiempo por palabra con alineación forzada y es de código abierto.
  - Las palabras con números o símbolos pueden quedar sin marca de tiempo.
  - La salida .ass se retiró en la v3, así que Claude tendría que generar el ASS con un script propio. https://github.com/m-bain/whisperX
  - Con ElevenLabs puedes saltarte Whisper si usas su salida con marcas de tiempo (no verificado en esta sesión).
  - Luego se queman con ffmpeg y libass, con las palabras enfatizadas en mayúsculas y otro color.
- **Remotion:** gratis para individuos y empresas de hasta 3 personas, con uso comercial. La licencia de empresa cuesta 25 USD por puesto al mes, o 0.01 USD por render con mínimo de 100 USD al mes. https://www.remotion.dev/docs/license/pricing.md

## 5. Música y efectos

- **YouTube Audio Library:** gratis y la más segura. YouTube dice que sus pistas "no serán reclamadas por Content ID" y que se pueden monetizar. Las pistas Creative Commons exigen crédito en la descripción. https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/3376882
- **Pixabay:** gratis y sin atribución obligatoria. https://pixabay.com/service/license-summary/
  - Algunos autores registran pistas en Content ID y puede tocar disputar reclamos con el certificado de licencia (fuente secundaria). https://www.foximusic.com/blog/need-background-music-that-wont-trigger-content-id/
- **Epidemic Sound:** sin plan gratis, con prueba de 30 días. La página oficial no me mostró precios. Terceros reportan Creator a 9.99 USD al mes con pago anual, o 17.99 mensual, con un canal por plataforma. https://www.epidemicsound.com/pricing/ y https://www.creatorstackclub.com/software/epidemic-sound
- **Uppbeat:** su página de precios devolvió error 429. Un comparativo propio habla de 9.99 USD al mes con pago anual y 17.99 mensual; no verificado. https://uppbeat.io/blog/royalty-free-and-copyright-free-music/uppbeat-vs-epidemic-sound-how-do-they-compare

## 6. Reglas de Roblox

- **Videos con avatares R6/R15:** el FAQ oficial del DevForum dice que las guías no restringen crear videos ni streams con ellos, y que "puedes seguir monetizando ese contenido (por ejemplo con ingresos de anuncios de YouTube)". https://devforum.roblox.com/t/update-to-roblox-licensing-program-brand-guidelines/1843674
- **Series o películas:** para un programa de TV o una película sí debes contactar a Roblox (mismo FAQ).
- **Nombre y logo:** si el canal usa "Roblox" o "Blox", debes decir que no está afiliado a Roblox. El logo no es de uso general en material creativo. Guías oficiales (no pude abrirlas por el bloqueo): https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/articles/115001708126
- **Música licenciada de Roblox:** la política permite ingresos por anuncios en capturas de video, pero no usarlas en "película, programa de TV, comercial o serie" (lo vi solo por resultado de búsqueda). https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/360038525351-Using-Licensed-Music-in-Videos
- **Ropa UGC y assets del marketplace en videos:** no encontré una cláusula específica; no verificado. Lo prudente es usar ropa propia o clásica, evitar marcas reales en la ropa y no usar audio del catálogo de Roblox en el video final.

## Stack mínimo recomendado

| Pieza | Nivel gratis | Nivel pago |
|---|---|---|
| Animación | Studio, Animation Editor, scripts de cámara vía MCP | Moon Animator 2, unos 30 USD una sola vez (no verificado) |
| Automatización | MCP integrado de Studio con Claude Code | Igual |
| Grabación | OBS | Igual |
| Voz | Tu voz, o ElevenLabs Free sin licencia comercial | ElevenLabs Starter 6 USD, o Creator 22 USD |
| Subtítulos y montaje | WhisperX, ASS y ffmpeg, o Remotion; DaVinci gratis | CapCut Standard o Pro, 10 a 20 USD (opcional) |
| Música | YouTube Audio Library, Pixabay | Epidemic o Uppbeat, 10 a 18 USD (opcional) |
| **Total al mes** | **0 USD** | **6 a 22 USD lo esencial; hasta unos 60 USD con todo** |

No incluye tu suscripción a Claude.

## Tiempo por video (estimación mía, no verificada)

- **Principiante:** 10 a 20 horas por video de 100 segundos y 25 a 30 tomas. La mayor parte se va en sets, caras y ajuste de cámara. Los primeros videos cuestan más porque armas la biblioteca reutilizable (sets, rigs, pack de caras, plantilla de subtítulos).
- **Con práctica:** 3 a 6 horas, con biblioteca hecha, guion y script director generados por Claude y subtítulos automatizados.

El cuello de botella será la revisión visual toma por toma. Es la misma limitación que reportan quienes construyen juegos con Claude por MCP.

## Lo que no pude verificar

- El flujo real y la voz de R6Rants.
